name: correctness
prompt: Correctness/logic: wrong branch, off-by-one, missing case, error-path that leaves state half-updated (pay-then-fail / partial write with no rollback), unchecked Err from a callee, ordering of state mutations vs. early return.

name: spec
prompt: Spec conformance: does this deviate from the CIP/whitepaper intent it claims to implement? Check field semantics, required checks, and whether a MUST rule is silently relaxed. Read the referenced spec text before judging.

name: cross-repo
prompt: Cross-repo/wire contract: any struct/enum/opcode/serialization that another repo (runner, wallet, indexer, gateway) or another code path must decode identically. Mismatched field order, added field not gated, opcode collision, in-memory-constructed instruction bypassing wire-decode bounds.

name: security
prompt: Security/authz/confidentiality: self-asserted authority, missing signature/binding check on a path that mirrors a guarded one, auth check present on sibling path but omitted here, secret/ciphertext exposure, SSRF/redirect, unbounded resource -> single-request amplification / DoS/halt.

name: econ
prompt: Economic conservation: value must be conserved across mint/burn/escrow/settlement/fee. Look for burn += full-amount regardless of actual debit, double settlement, non-idempotent settlement, mint into a sink, fee charged but service fails, escrow going negative.

name: determinism
prompt: Consensus determinism: does any byte entering state_root / receipt_root / logs_root / bloom / block digest depend on per-validator local state (wall-clock, cache warmth, object identity, iteration order, uptime)? Does an added consensus field change bytes for existing/default inputs (mixed-version fork, flag-day)? Attribution/provenance shifts that move what is committed.
